title: Picking columns

cells.text: Most of the time you only need a few columns. This lesson shows how to pick them.

cells.prompt: Press Run to load the games table.
cells.code:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv("games.csv")
df.head()

cells.text: To pick **one** column, put its name in quotes inside square brackets: `df["title"]`. One column on its own is called a **Series**: a single column with the row labels on the left.

cells.prompt: Press Run to pick just the title column.
Replace ___ with "genre" (with the quotes) to pick the genre column, then press Run.
hints: Column names are text, so they need quotes.

cells.text: Column names must match **exactly**, capital letters included. The column is called title, all lowercase.

cells.prompt: Notice the capital T this time. What will happen? Pick one, then press Run.

cells.text: That's a **KeyError**: Python couldn't find a column called Title. When you see one, check the spelling and capitals of the column name.

To pick **several** columns, put a list of names inside the brackets: `df[["title", "price"]]`. That's **double** brackets: the outer ones mean "pick", and the inner ones hold the list of names. The result is a smaller table (a DataFrame).

cells.prompt: Press Run to pick the title and price columns.
Replace ___ with "rating" to pick the title and rating columns, then press Run.
hints: Add the column name in quotes, inside the inner brackets.

cells.text: You can add `.head()` or `.tail()` straight after picking, to see only some rows: `df[["title", "price"]].head(2)`.

cells.prompt: Your turn: show the title, genre and rating columns for the first 5 games. Pick the 3 columns with double brackets, then add .head() at the end.
hints: Put the 3 names in quotes, separated by commas, inside double brackets. Then add .head()

cells.prompt: Last one: show the title and release_year columns for the last 4 games only.
hints: Pick the 2 columns with double brackets, then add .tail() with a number.

recap: df["name"] picks one column (a Series). df[["a", "b"]] picks several (a DataFrame). Names must match exactly, or you get a KeyError.
